title: Prompt injection is why I moved my agents to the cloud
overlay_title: Why I run coding agents in the cloud
note: Full arc: local-agent risk -> the hidden-text attack -> names it -> cloud fixes it.
post_title: Prompt injection is the reason my coding agents live in the cloud
description: A local coding agent can read your files, your passwords and your secrets. All it takes is a website with hidden text telling it to send them somewhere. That's prompt injection, and it's why I moved my agents into cloud containers.

title: Limit the blast radius on every API key you hand an agent
note: Opens on the thesis. An earlier cut carried ~44s of setup about vaults and secrets proxies; self-contained but too slow for a short, so the nuance moves to the post body and the clip keeps the two concrete controls.
post_title: You cannot stop an agent leaking a secret. Limit the blast radius instead
description: Vaults and secrets proxies still lose to a determined agent, so stop trying to make leaks impossible and make them cheap instead: a $5 spend cap on every API key, and a 30-day expiry so a key stolen off a server six months from now is already worthless.

title: The prompt that stops AI burying you in walls of text
note: Shortest clip, single quotable prompt. Strong standalone.
post_title: The prompt that stops AI burying you in walls of text
description: Tell the agent you are a human with a limited attention span and it may only put one decision in front of you per turn. It turns an overwhelming markdown dump into a conversation you can actually follow.

title: Be something other than a software developer first
note: Hook-first: opens on the thesis, not the question that prompted it.
post_title: Be something other than a software developer first
description: Everybody in software builds dev tools, because those are the problems they know. That is a market with a million competitors. The problems worth solving are in whatever other field you already understand.

title: The more niche the market, the better
note: Honest about the ceiling - not scalable, but it pays. Ends on a clean maxim.
post_title: The more niche the market, the better
description: Google and Intuit are not incentivised to chase your niche. You will never build a billion dollar business in cross stitch or religious history, but you can build one that pays you very well.

title: Nobody is using job websites anymore
overlay_title: Applying online is a losing game
note: Internal cut drops an off-hand line about scammers by nationality; the clip keeps the argument and lands on 'it is who you know'.
post_title: Nobody is using job websites anymore
description: Post a job now and you get thousands of AI-written applications nobody can sort through. Applying online has become a losing game, which makes who you know matter more than it ever has.

title: Tell the agent to attack your own pull request
overlay_title: Make the agent attack your PR
note: Internal cut skips the parallel-models tangent so the clip is one idea: adversarial review, then loop it.
post_title: Tell the agent to attack your own pull request
description: Do not ask an agent to review your PR. Tell it to attack the PR: write four tests that break the system and find the holes in your design. Then loop it until it stops finding anything new.

title: Detailed up-front planning beats agile now
overlay_title: Why I plan up front again
note: Contrarian hook: 'more markdown than code'. Old advice -> why it changed.
post_title: Detailed up-front planning beats agile now
description: Planning used to be wasted effort because plans broke the moment you hit the code. Agents are strong enough now that a very detailed spec written up front pays for itself. My job is more markdown than code.
